records.tss_identity_note: Named in IMO COLREG.2/Circ.59 (MSC 83, 2007) as amended scheme with special provisions for the North Hinder to German Bight tanker route, implemented 1 May 2008 (S1); listed in IMO Ships' Routeing 2008 (S27) and Transportstyrelsen 2017 list (S4). German statute designates it a deep-water route (Tiefwasserweg) mandatory for large tankers (S6 Nr. 6). MSC 109 adopted a revised containership recommendation covering it from 1 July 2025 (lead S5). No evidence of renaming or restructuring by recent IMO amendments was found.
records.vts_relationship_basis: AnlBV Anlage Nr. 3.1 requires ships approaching the Inner German Bight from the west to report to 'German Bight Traffic' at 007° 10' E 'unabhängig davon, ob das Verkehrstrennungsgebiet German Bight Western Approach benutzt wird' (S6); Nr. 5.1 states traffic is monitored under maritime traffic safety. Coverage evidenced for the eastern part of the scheme and its approach into the Inner German Bight; the western extent of the scheme relative to the VTS area was not verified.
records.reporting_relationship_basis: National mandatory report (AnlBV Nr. 3.1) at 007° 10' E for ships and tows over 300 GT, expressly regardless of use of this TSS (S6). Not an IMO-adopted SRS.
records.applicability_notes: Report: over 300 GT. Mandatory use of the TSS (AnlBV Nr. 6): oil tankers over 10,000 GT, NLS Z tankers over 10,000 GT, NLS X/Y tankers over 5,000 GT, gas tankers over 10,000 GT approaching or leaving the Inner German Bight from the west. Mandatory route for tankers from North Hinder to the German Bight applies to oil tankers 10,000 GT and over, chemical/NLS tankers 5,000 GT (X/Y) or 10,000 GT (Z) and over, and gas carriers 10,000 GT and over (S1, annex 4).
records.complexity_reason: National mandatory reporting plus national mandatory-use rule, IMO mandatory tanker route and 2025 containership recommendation overlap; cross-border Dutch/German routeing context.
records.open_questions: Exact westward extent of the scheme and whether any part lies in Netherlands waters not verified. IMO text of the 2024 containership recommendation (MSC 109) not retrieved. No evidence found of any recent IMO renaming of German TSS, but Circ. texts after 2016 were not all retrieved.
records.research_effort: approx 14 web actions (shared across German records)

records.tss_identity_note: Listed as 'Elbe approach' in IMO Ships' Routeing 2008 (S27) and the Transportstyrelsen 2017 list of IMO schemes (S4). Adopting and latest amending circular not retrieved.
records.vts_relationship_basis: Cuxhaven VTS is responsible for the Elbe 'im Bereich der Elbeansteuerung' (Elbe approach) (S9); the GDWS Bekanntmachung sets the Cuxhaven Elbe Traffic area from buoy Nordergründe-Nord (008° E), with outbound reports there to German Bight Traffic on VHF 80 (S7). Coverage is of the direct approach; the TSS lanes themselves are in the Inner German Bight covered by German Bight Traffic, but the exact TSS-to-sector boundary was not verified.
records.reporting_relationship_basis: SeeSchStrO § 58 position report at NGN (008° E) to Cuxhaven Elbe Traffic inbound and German Bight Traffic outbound (S7); AnlBV Nr. 3.1 entry report for ships entering the Inner German Bight from west or north (S6). National, not IMO.
records.applicability_notes: SeeSchStrO § 58: vessels of 50 m LOA or more and ships under § 30(1). AnlBV: over 300 GT.
records.complexity_reason: Two VTS services and two national reporting regimes meet at the seaward end of the Elbe.
records.open_questions: Adopting IMO instrument and current chart geometry not retrieved; confirm whether the TSS lies seaward of NGN (German Bight Traffic sector) or partly within Cuxhaven Elbe Traffic sector.
records.research_effort: approx 5 web actions (plus shared German sources)

records.tss_identity_note: Listed as 'Jade approach' in IMO Ships' Routeing 2008 (S27) and Transportstyrelsen 2017 list (S4). WSV describes it as the link between Terschelling-German Bight and the Western Approach giving access to Weser and Jade from the north (S11). German statute places a pilot transfer position 'im Verkehrstrennungsgebiet Jade Approach' within the Inner German Bight (S6 Nr. 8).
records.vts_relationship_basis: AnlBV Nr. 8 locates the scheme in the Inner German Bight outside the territorial sea; Nr. 5.1 states traffic there is monitored under maritime traffic safety and Nr. 3.1 routes reports to German Bight Traffic (S6). German Bight Traffic monitors the inner German Bight from Borkum to Helgoland (S8).
records.reporting_relationship_basis: AnlBV Nr. 3.1 report at 54° 20' N or 007° 10' E; SeeSchStrO § 58 entry report at 54° 15' N west of Helgoland to German Bight Traffic (S6, S7).
records.applicability_notes: AnlBV: over 300 GT. SeeSchStrO § 58: 50 m or more. Compulsory pilotage from the Jade Approach transfer position for large tankers, bulk carriers and other ships per AnlBV Nr. 8 (S6).
records.complexity_reason: National reporting, VTS and offshore pilotage obligations combine; single VTS.
records.open_questions: Adopting IMO instrument and any recent amendments not retrieved.
records.research_effort: approx 3 web actions (plus shared German sources)

records.tss_identity_note: Amended by COLREG.2/Circ.59 (MSC 83, implemented 1 May 2008) (S1); listed in Ships' Routeing 2008 (S27) and Transportstyrelsen 2017 list (S4). MSC 109 containership recommendation from 1 July 2025 (lead S5).
records.vts_relationship_basis: Bekanntmachung 19.1.4 and 19.1.5 require vessels using the TSS 'Terschelling - German Bight' and its inshore traffic zone to report to German Bight Traffic at Borkumriff buoy (VHF 79) and at TG 17/C eastbound (VHF 80) (S7). This establishes coverage of the German (eastern) part only. For the Dutch part: No Dutch VTS was found whose defined area covers this offshore scheme. The Netherlands Coastguard performs Vessel Traffic Monitoring (VTMon) and distinguishes VTS as provided by traffic centres (S14, S15); VTMon is recorded as a lead only, not as a VTS.
records.reporting_relationship_basis: SeeSchStrO § 58 entry and position reports (vessels 50 m or more) and AnlBV Nr. 3.1 (over 300 GT) apply on the German part (S6, S7). National, not IMO. No mandatory reporting identified for the Dutch part.
records.voluntary_reporting: Netherlands Coastguard broadcasts wave-height advice for container ships in TSS Terschelling-German Bight and may advise the northern route; advice is not binding (S13).
records.applicability_notes: Mandatory route for tankers from North Hinder to the German Bight applies to oil tankers 10,000 GT and over, chemical/NLS tankers 5,000 GT (X/Y) or 10,000 GT (Z) and over, and gas carriers 10,000 GT and over (S1, annex 4). Coastguard advice targets container ships 100 to 200 m at 3 m waves and over 200 m at 4 m waves (S13).
records.complexity_reason: Cross-border scheme: German VTS and national reporting on eastern part, no VTS evidenced on Dutch part, plus mandatory tanker route and containership advice.
records.open_questions: Exact boundary between German Bight Traffic coverage and the Dutch part not verified. Rijkswaterstaat Brandaris (Terschelling) VTS designation could not be read (officielebekendmakingen.nl returned HTTP 403); search snippets indicate its area is the Terschelling zeegat approach, not the TSS.

records.official_name: Vlieland North (part of 'Off Vlieland, Vlieland North and Vlieland Junction')
records.tss_identity_note: COLREG.2/Circ.59 (MSC 83, implemented 1 May 2008) amended the special provisions of 'Off Vlieland, Vlieland North and Vlieland Junction' (S1). IMO Ships' Routeing 2008 treats these as one routeing system entry (S27). Component of the same system as TSS-0051.
records.vts_relationship_basis: No Dutch VTS was found whose defined area covers this offshore scheme. The Netherlands Coastguard performs Vessel Traffic Monitoring (VTMon) and distinguishes VTS as provided by traffic centres (S14, S15); VTMon is recorded as a lead only, not as a VTS.
records.reporting_relationship_basis: No IMO-adopted mandatory ship reporting system or national mandatory reporting specific to this scheme was found. Netherlands Coastguard states it 'has no powers to impose traffic directions' (S13). A failed search is not proof of absence.
records.applicability_notes: Mandatory route for tankers from North Hinder to the German Bight applies to oil tankers 10,000 GT and over, chemical/NLS tankers 5,000 GT (X/Y) or 10,000 GT (Z) and over, and gas carriers 10,000 GT and over (S1, annex 4).
records.complexity_reason: Part of a multi-component routeing system linked to the IMO mandatory tanker route; no VTS or reporting identified.
records.open_questions: Duplicate/grouping: likely to merge with TSS-0051 under 'Off Vlieland, Vlieland North and Vlieland Junction'. Current Dutch legal text (puc.overheid.nl) returned HTTP 403.

records.vts_relationship_basis: No Dutch VTS was found whose defined area covers this offshore scheme. The Netherlands Coastguard performs Vessel Traffic Monitoring (VTMon) and distinguishes VTS as provided by traffic centres (S14, S15); VTMon is recorded as a lead only, not as a VTS.
records.reporting_relationship_basis: No IMO-adopted mandatory ship reporting system or national mandatory reporting specific to this scheme was found. Netherlands Coastguard states it 'has no powers to impose traffic directions' (S13). A failed search is not proof of absence.
records.voluntary_reporting: Coastguard container-ship wave advice applies to the southern route north of the West Frisian Islands (S13); relationship to this specific scheme not stated.
records.applicability_notes: Mandatory route for tankers from North Hinder to the German Bight applies to oil tankers 10,000 GT and over, chemical/NLS tankers 5,000 GT (X/Y) or 10,000 GT (Z) and over, and gas carriers 10,000 GT and over (S1, annex 4).
records.complexity_reason: Multi-component system, mandatory tanker route and containership recommendation; no VTS identified.

Den Helder port VTS not researched for coverage of this scheme.

records.tss_identity_note: New scheme adopted by MSC 91 and circulated as COLREG.2/Circ.64 (2012), implemented 1 August 2013, per Transportstyrelsen list (S4); associated precautionary areas in SN.1/Circ.317 (S4). Separate IMO deep-water route leading to IJmuiden listed in Ships' Routeing 2008 (S27). Circ.64 text not retrieved.
records.vts_relationship_basis: VTS North Sea Canal Area covers 'the approaches to IJmuiden ... within a 12-nautical-mile radius ... including the extended IJ-geul deep water channel' (S12). The source does not state that the TSS lanes lie within this area; the extended IJ-geul is a separate IMO deep-water route. VTS named as a strong lead; overlap with the TSS needs chart verification.
records.reporting_relationship_basis: No IMO or national mandatory reporting system specific to the TSS found. Within the VTS area there are ordinary VTS reporting duties: report on arrival at 12 nm to Sector IJmuiden VHF 61 and to IJmuiden Approaches VHF 07 'as soon as VHF contact is possible' (S12). These are VTS reporting duties, recorded separately.
records.applicability_notes: VTS reporting and listening watch apply to vessels in the VTS area per S12.
records.complexity_reason: TSS, deep-water route, precautionary areas and a port VTS with sector structure; overlap to be confirmed.
records.open_questions: Retrieve Circ.64 annex or chart INT 1418 to test whether any TSS lane lies within 12 nm of the breakwaters or on the extended IJ-geul. Dutch 2020 to 2023 Notices to Mariners (defensie.nl) returned 404.

records.tss_identity_note: Existence of a TSS 'Off Brown Ridge' is indicated only by leads: Wikipedia list 'Brown Ridge' (S30) and search snippets describing a deep-water route linking TSS Off Brown Ridge to TSS West Friesland and the 1 August 2013 Dutch re-routeing. Not found in Ships' Routeing 2008 contents (S27) or Transportstyrelsen 2017 list (S4) as a separate entry; may be a component of 'Off Friesland' or of the 2013 Dutch routeing package. records.reporting_relationship_basis: No IMO-adopted mandatory ship reporting system or national mandatory reporting specific to this scheme was found. Netherlands Coastguard states it 'has no powers to impose traffic directions' (S13). A failed search is not proof of absence.

records.complexity_reason: Component of a multi-scheme routeing system with deep-water routes and tanker routeing provisions.
records.open_questions: Grouping: TSS-0055, TSS-0056, TSS-0057 and TSS-0058 appear to be components of the single IMO routeing system 'Off Friesland'; consider merging.

records.tss_identity_note: Amended by COLREG.2/Circ.51 (MSC 75), implemented 1 May 2003 (S18); further amended by COLREG.2/Circ.64 (MSC 91), implemented 1 June 2013 per search result (Circ.64 text not retrieved). French ministry 2024 confirms DST Ouessant under CROSS Corsen (S19).
records.vts_relationship_basis: IMO MSC.52(66): OUESSREP area 'covers a circular area 35 miles in radius centred on the Ile d'Ouessant' and 'The TSS covers the entire area'; shore authority is the Corsen/Ouessant VTS 'Ushant Traffic' at CROSS Corsen, VHF 13 (S16). French ministry 2024: 'DST Ouessant : zone de compétences CROSS Corsen' (S19).
records.reporting_relationship_basis: OUESSREP, IMO-adopted SOLAS mandatory ship reporting system (MSC.52(66), amended MSC.251(83) in force 1 May 2008) covering the TSS (S16, S17); French 2024 publication confirms Channel CROSS monitor ships over 300 UMS 'soumis à un compte rendu obligatoire' (S19).
records.applicability_notes: Ships of more than 300 GRT (S16). Report content amended 2008 to include bunker quantity for ships carrying over 5,000 t bunkers (S17).
records.complexity_reason: Single VTS with IMO mandatory reporting; well documented.
records.open_questions: A current CROSS Corsen or Premar Atlantique page with VHF channels was not retrieved; channels are from the 1996 IMO text.

records.tss_identity_note: Originally adopted by A.767(18) (cited in S20); amended by A.957(23), implemented 1 June 2004, adding lanes for ships carrying dangerous or pollutant cargoes in bulk (S21). Listed in Ships' Routeing 2008 (S27).
records.vts_relationship_basis: MSC.63(67): FINREP area 'includes the traffic separation scheme "off Finisterre"' and ships 'shall report to the Finisterre Traffic VTS' (S20). The amended 2004 outer southbound lane reaches 010° 13.7' W (S21), slightly west of the 1996 FINREP limit (010° 10' W), so coverage of the outermost lane is not evidenced.
records.reporting_relationship_basis: FINREP, IMO-adopted mandatory SRS in force 3 June 1997 (S20).
records.applicability_notes: FINREP: ships of 50 m LOA or more; ships carrying hazardous or potentially polluting cargo; tows over 50 m; smaller vessels fishing in or using lanes in emergency (S20). Dangerous cargo ships use designated outer lanes (S21).
records.complexity_reason: VTS with IMO mandatory reporting; cargo-based lane allocation; possible mismatch of FINREP limit with amended TSS.
records.open_questions: Salvamento Marítimo website returned HTTP 503/TLS failure, so current VTS name and VHF channel not confirmed from operator; only a 2025 news lead (S22). Check whether FINREP geographical limits were amended after 2004.

records.tss_identity_note: Amended by MSC 79 (December 2004) with entry into force 1 July 2005 (S23 preamble) and again by COLREG.2/Circ.61 (MSC 87), implemented 1 December 2010 (S26). Established in Portuguese law as 'EST do cabo da Roca' (S23 art. 4).
records.vts_relationship_basis: DL 263/2009 art. 6 defines the coastal VTS area (west limit 10° 14' W north of 38° 41' N) and art. 10(4) gives the CCTMC supervision of 'regras aplicáveis aos esquemas de separação de tráfego' (S24); DL 198/2006 art. 9 assigns TSS enforcement to the national VTS authority (S23). All Circ.61 positions of the scheme (westmost 010° 13.78' W) fall inside the statutory VTS area on coordinate comparison (S26).
records.reporting_relationship_basis: COPREP (MSC.278(85), in force 1 June 2009) area bounded west by 010° 14' W and to the south-west by the line 38° 41' N 010° 14' W to 36° 30' N 009° 35' W (S25); the scheme lies inside on coordinate comparison. Reports to Roca Control.
records.voluntary_reporting: COPREP invites any other vessel type to participate voluntarily (S25).
records.applicability_notes: COPREP and VTS: ships of 300 GT or above, dangerous/polluting cargo, passenger ships, tows over 100 m, fishing vessels 24 m or more (S24, S25). Separate lanes for ships carrying dangerous or pollutant cargoes in bulk (S26).
records.complexity_reason: Single national coastal VTS with IMO mandatory reporting and cargo-based lanes.
records.open_questions: DL 263/2009 cites IPTM; current operating authority (DGRM) not confirmed from a DGRM page. Coverage relies on coordinate comparison.

records.official_name: Western Traffic Separation Scheme (between Grand Canary and Tenerife), part of the Canary Islands schemes
records.tss_identity_note: New scheme adopted by MSC 81 in COLREG.2/Circ.57 (26 May 2006), implemented 1 December 2006 (S28). Listed as 'Between Grand Canary and Tenerife' in Ships' Routeing 2008 (S27).
records.vts_relationship_basis: No designated VTS found. Primary sources name MRCC Tenerife as recipient of voluntary TSS notifications and CANREP reports (S28, S29), but describe it as an MRCC, not a VTS. MRCC recorded as lead (SVC-es-canarias-mrcc).
records.reporting_relationship_basis: CANREP area is a polygon along the outer limit of the territorial sea enclosing the archipelago, so inter-island waters including this scheme lie inside (S29, section 2.1). Applies only to specified heavy-oil tankers.
records.voluntary_reporting: Ships may notify entry to and departure from the TSS via MRCC Tenerife on VHF 16 (S28).
records.applicability_notes: CANREP: tankers of 600 dwt and above carrying heavy crude, heavy fuel oil, bitumen or tar, transiting or trading inter-island (S29).
records.complexity_reason: Narrow-scope IMO mandatory reporting plus voluntary TSS notification; no VTS.
records.open_questions: Check whether Salvamento Marítimo operates a VTS function for the Canary TSS (website unavailable). CANREP coverage of the TSS rests on the polygon description; the chartlet was not inspected.

records.official_name: Eastern Traffic Separation Scheme (between Grand Canary and Fuerteventura), part of the Canary Islands schemes
records.tss_identity_note: New scheme in COLREG.2/Circ.57, implemented 1 December 2006 (S28); includes a precautionary area and inshore traffic zone. Listed in Ships' Routeing 2008 (S27).
records.vts_relationship_basis: As TSS-0064; MRCC Las Palmas receives voluntary notifications (S28); no VTS designation found.
records.reporting_relationship_basis: Inside the CANREP polygon (S29); ships entering east of 015° 30' W report to MRCC Las Palmas.
records.voluntary_reporting: Ships may notify entry to and departure from the TSS via MRCC Las Palmas on VHF 16 (S28).
records.complexity_reason: As TSS-0064.
records.open_questions: As TSS-0064.

batch_audits.evidence_check: Each 'Confirmed present' re-checked against passages: German Bight Traffic coverage rests on AnlBV Nr. 3.1/5.1/8 (S6) and GDWS Bekanntmachung 19.1 (S7), both statutory; Cuxhaven Elbe Traffic on S9 and S7. Downgraded nothing, but TSS-0047 and TSS-0046 bases are worded as approach/part coverage.
batch_audits.classification_check: German reporting is national mandatory (AnlBV, SeeSchStrO § 58), not IMO SOLAS V/11; classified 'Confirmed present' as national mandatory reporting per brief. Dutch part of TSS-0049 has no VTS or reporting evidence; Coastguard VTMon treated as lead, not VTS.
batch_audits.duplication_check: German Bight Traffic is one service across TSS-0046/0048/0049 and part of 0047 (same key). TSS-0050 is a component of 'Off Vlieland, Vlieland North and Vlieland Junction' shared with TSS-0051.
batch_audits.unresolved_items: TSS-0050 VTS and reporting; Dutch part of TSS-0049; exact extent of TSS-0046 west of 007° 10' E; no IMO text for 2024 containership recommendation; no evidence of recent German TSS renaming found.

batch_audits.evidence_check: No 'Confirmed present' findings in this batch. Port of Amsterdam VTS (S12) confirmed as a service but not linked to TSS-0053 because the passage does not establish TSS coverage.
batch_audits.classification_check: All Dutch offshore records left 'Unresolved' for VTS and reporting; none marked 'Confirmed absent' because no complete authoritative list states absence.
batch_audits.duplication_check: TSS-0051 duplicates the routeing system of TSS-0050. TSS-0055 is a component of 'Off Friesland' with TSS-0056, 0057 and probably 0058. TSS-0054 may also belong to a wider Dutch system.
batch_audits.unresolved_items: Identity of Off Brown Ridge (TSS-0054) is provisional; COLREG.2/Circ.64 not retrieved; IJmuiden TSS overlap with 12 nm VTS area to be verified on chart.

batch_audits.evidence_check: TSS-0059: VTS and OUESSREP rest on IMO MSC.52(66) passage stating the TSS covers the reporting area and naming the Corsen/Ouessant VTS, reinforced by 2024 French ministry text. TSS-0060: VTS and FINREP rest on MSC.63(67) passage naming the TSS and Finisterre Traffic VTS; caveat recorded that the 2004 outer lane extends 3.7' west of the FINREP limit.
batch_audits.classification_check: OUESSREP and FINREP are IMO-adopted mandatory SRS. Dutch components (0056 to 0058) left Unresolved.
batch_audits.duplication_check: TSS-0056/0057 (and 0058) are components of 'Off Friesland' with TSS-0055; 'North Friesland' and 'East Friesland' are Dutch offshore schemes, not German Frisian coastal schemes.
batch_audits.unresolved_items: Current operator pages for CROSS Corsen and Salvamento Marítimo not retrieved (503/TLS failure for Salvamento Marítimo); Off Botney Ground currency.

batch_audits.evidence_check: TSS-0061/0062 VTS rests on Portuguese statutes DL 263/2009 art. 6 and 10(4) and DL 198/2006 art. 9, plus coordinate comparison with COLREG.2/Circ.61; COPREP on MSC.278(85) area plus coordinate comparison. TSS-0064/0065 CANREP rests on MSC.213(81) area description enclosing the archipelago. All retained, with basis stated.
batch_audits.classification_check: COPREP and CANREP are IMO-adopted mandatory SRS; CANREP scope is narrow (heavy-oil tankers). Canary TSS voluntary notification recorded separately. Canary VTS left Unresolved: MRCCs are not evidenced as VTS.
batch_audits.duplication_check: Same Portuguese coastal VTS key for TSS-0061 and 0062. Canary schemes are two components of one IMO entry 'The Canary Islands' (COLREG.2/Circ.57) but listed separately in Ships' Routeing; kept separate.
batch_audits.unresolved_items: Banco del Hoyo (TSS-0063) location and currency; Canary VTS status; current Portuguese authority (DGRM) not confirmed from its own page.

method_notes: Access problems: puc.overheid.nl (Dutch NSI legal texts on TSS), officielebekendmakingen.nl and digitale-bibliothek.bsh.bund.de returned HTTP 403 or bot challenges; Dutch Notices to Mariners PDFs on english.defensie.nl for 2017 to 2023 returned 404; salvamentomaritimo.es returned 503 via WebFetch and failed TLS verification via curl; NOAA copy of COLREG.2/Circ.64 redirects. Useful sources: German statutes on gesetze-im-internet.de (AnlBV Anlage) and ELWIS SeeSchStrO § 58 page, which reproduces the WSD/GDWS Bekanntmachungen with VTS areas, VHF channels and TSS-specific reporting points; WSA Verkehrszentralen pages; Portuguese decree-laws hosted by marinha.pt; IMO resolution PDFs on wwwcdn.imo.org (MSC resolutions downloadable); IMO COLREG.2 circulars mirrored by Shanghai Maritime University (cimrc.shmtu.edu.cn) and other administrations; Transportstyrelsen list of IMO routeing measures (2017) for adopting-instrument history; kustwacht.nl for Dutch Coastguard role. Method suggestions: obtain the current IMO Ships' Routeing (Part B) and COLREG.2/Circ.64 onwards (Circ.68 to latest) to settle Brown Ridge, Botney Ground, Banco del Hoyo and any post-2020 German Bight changes; merge 'Off Friesland' components (0055 to 0058) and 'Off Vlieland' components (0050/0051); treat German AnlBV and SeeSchStrO reporting as national mandatory reporting, distinct from IMO SRS. Third-party hosted copies of IMO circulars were classed Primary as IMO texts; reviewers may prefer to re-source them from IMODOCS.
